bases.source:
At the interim analysis cut-off (29 March 2019),
148 patients in cohort A and 67 in cohort B were
continuing to receive study treatment (online
Supplemental Figure 1). In cohort A, 91 patients
(44.0%) in the abemaciclib arm and 65 patients
(65.7%) in the placebo arm had discontinued
treatment. In cohort B, 50 patients (48.1%) in
the abemaciclib arm and 40 patients (75.5%) in
the placebo arm had discontinued treatment. The
majority of patients discontinued treatment due
to progressive disease. The comparable median
number of cycles received per patient in cohort A
(15 for the abemaciclib arm and 13 for the pla-
cebo arm) was due to the limited duration of fol-
low-up, while in cohort B, the median number of
cycles was 9.5 for the abemaciclib arm and 6.0 for
the placebo arm. More patients had dose reduc-
tions or omissions in the abemaciclib arm (cohort
A: 40.5%/62.4%; cohort B: 39.4%/52.9%) than
the placebo arm (cohort A: 2.0%/30.3%; cohort
B: 1.9%/17.0%).
Efficacy
The interim analysis occurred after 119 PFS
events were observed in the ITT population in
cohort A [66 (31.9%) of 207 patients in the abe-
maciclib arm and 53 (53.5%) of 99 patients in
the placebo arm] and the median follow-up was
approximately 16 months in both arms. The
study met its primary endpoint with an investiga-
tor-assessed PFS hazard ratio of 0.499 (95% CI
0.346-0.719; p = 0.0001) in cohort A. Median
PFS was not reached in the abemaciclib arm and
was 14.7 months in the placebo arm (Figure 2A).

Supplementary Figure 1, Trial Profile. Cohort A: 207 assigned abemaciclib + NSAI; 2 not treated (2 inclusion criteria not met); 91 discontinued treatment (57 disease progression, 20 adverse event, 7 withdrawal by patient, 3 physician decision, 2 death, 2 protocol deviation); 114 on treatment at data cutoff; 207 in ITT analysis. Placebo + NSAI: 99 assigned; 65 discontinued treatment (51 disease progression, 8 withdrawal by patient, 3 adverse event, 2 lost to follow-up, 1 death); 34 on treatment at data cutoff; 99 in ITT analysis.

bases.stopping_rationale: Inspected the article's outcome/disposition text and supplement flow figure. A scoped search attempt failed with source/search projection integrity error and produced no search result (not a no-hit). Historical registry projection raw bytes unavailable; did not replace it or access network.
bases.unresolved_premise: Outcome availability for all or nearly all randomized participants is unresolved.

answers.justification: For the approved cohort A investigator-assessed PFS at 29 March 2019, the article reports 119 events among 207 abemaciclib+NSAI and 99 placebo+NSAI participants and ITT analysis, but event and analysis denominators do not establish the number with outcome ascertainment. The flow diagram identifies two placebo participants as lost to follow-up, while treatment discontinuation/on-treatment counts are not outcome availability. No arm-specific PFS observed/censored accounting was established.
unknowns: Actual outcome-observed/censored counts at this interim cutoff by randomized arm; whether follow-up continued after treatment discontinuation; reasons and timing of missing PFS observations.

bases.stopping_rationale: Bounded article and supplement review; lexical search was blocked by integrity failure; registry raw projection unavailable.
bases.unresolved_premise: No reassuring missing-outcome analysis was identified in inspected accessible text.

answers.justification: The inspected report gives the ITT analysis and primary PFS estimate, but these do not demonstrate protection from bias due to unobserved outcomes. Available passages disclose no bias-correcting analysis or sensitivity analysis over plausible missing-outcome assumptions. This is absence of reassurance, not proof bias occurred.
unknowns: Whether an uninspected analysis addressed plausible missing PFS outcomes.

answers.justification: The evidence does not establish that the two lost-to-follow-up placebo participants' missingness likely depended on true PFS, nor does it document a benign reason. Other treatment discontinuations are not shown to represent loss of outcome follow-up.
unknowns: Missingness reasons/rates and follow-up after treatment stopping by group; evidence of outcome-related loss.
